read_only_proof: This HARNESS is read-only — it opens each member's existing store and reads it. The store it read was re-indexed by hand immediately before the run (see generation.index_built_on): all 84 members, `logos index` per member from a binary built on this worktree's branch point (merged sprint-69 Iteration 1), exit 0 on every one, 0 failures. 25 member stores were rewritten and 59 were already current, which is what an incremental re-index over an already-warm estate does. It is stated here rather than implied, because a figure whose index generation is unattributable is the defect this artifact exists to prevent. Two readings of this generation were taken by two sessions: S-398 T2 re-indexed all 84 members (exit 0 on every one; 7,895 files / 93,838 nodes / 102,427 edges in 67 s) and read the estate twice, 34 minutes apart, with all 1034 reference rows byte-identical between them; S-403 T1 then re-read the same store. The two agree on every figure except `resolved_cross_service_edges`, which is the defect S-403 T1 fixed and is recorded in `generations`. [APPENDED 2026-09-18, S-420 T2.] This harness is still read-only and still indexes nothing. The generation it now reads was written by a separate, human-gated re-enrolment of the 84 members at logos 1.4.12 on 2026-09-17. One side effect is recorded so a later reader does not discover it as a surprise: reading the estate with a binary whose index generation differs from the enrolled one re-syncs every member store (last_sync_at and db_size_bytes both move). That sync changed no figure — the same estate read with the 1.4.12 binary and with the sprint-71 one gave byte-identical coverage payloads — but the stores now carry a sprint-71 sync stamp, which is not a re-index of content.

generation.why: Refusal rows, configuration-bound targets and committed topic values are all written at INDEX time, as are the tree-sitter invocation queries S-402 T1 narrowed. This store was re-enrolled on 2026-09-17 from a 1.4.12 binary, so it holds S-374, S-397 T1, S-398 T1, S-402 T1, S-399, S-405, S-409 and S-410. The contract-surface half is unchanged across every generation recorded here, which is what makes the comparison sound. The harness's cross-check moved to the egress DENOMINATOR, which a resolution does not move.
generation.refresh_procedure: At the sprint-review human gate, on a binary built from this sprint's merged main: (1) `logos init --workspace --yes` at ~/source/pec-services if the estate is not enrolled — this re-enrols the root and spawns the detached warm supervisor that indexes the 84 members (~43 s to return; a root `logos index` covers the ROOT ONLY, 3 files, and that is correct). On an already-enrolled estate a per-member `logos index` sweep is enough and is what the reading above used. (2) Wait for `.logos.workspace.warm.json` to report every member warm. (3) Re-run this harness with `LOGOS_REF_WORKSPACE=~/source/pec-services LOGOS_BASELINE_WRITE=1 cargo test -p logos-core --test coverage_headline_baseline -- --nocapture`, which rewrites the `measurement` block below. (4) Restate the `deltas` entries whose status is `pending-reindex` as `observed`, with the figures the run produced. (5) Re-record the estate figures restated in prose OUTSIDE this artifact — nothing tests them, so they rot silently: docs/howto/commands.md (worked examples + the config-bound paragraph), logos-core/src/federation/coverage.rs (`by_intake` and `resolved_cross_service_edges` field docs), logos-core/src/federation/reach.rs (`resolved_cross_service_edges` and `spec_conformance_measured` field docs), mcp/src/server.rs (both tool descriptions), web/src/api_v1.rs, web/ui/src/api/types.ts. (6) Commit the artifact and the finding beside it.
generation.figures_the_refresh_would_change: DISCHARGED — every figure below is observed rather than predicted, and three successive refreshes are now on the record. The third (this one) is the re-enrolment the S-399 delta was waiting for. Its movement decomposes and is NEVER netted: by_intake.invocation.bound 15 -> 45 is +27 broker rows (S-409/S-410, a population that did not exist in this payload) and +3 HTTP rows (S-399's three sites and S-405's six, of which three land in `bound` and six in `ambiguous`); invocation `unbound` 79 -> 43 is the other side of the same two movements plus the broker arm's own `topic-not-literal` residue falling 54 -> 27; the egress denominator is UNCHANGED at 117, so egress_resolution moved on its numerator alone this time (0.128 -> 0.385). S-420 T1 is in the reading binary and changes NOTHING here: the same estate read with and without its bridge arm on 2026-09-18 produced a byte-identical payload, while coverage.bridge_invocation_edges moved 33 -> 51. That paired reading lives in config_bound_admission.rs and its artifact, the single home for it.

headline_reading: FIFTY-ONE cross-service edges in this estate are resolved from a captured call site, over 117 captured egress sites (0.385) — while spec_conformance_ratio reads 0.365 on the same data and the pooled `bound` reads 126. 81 of those 126 are contract-surface matches (an OpenAPI operation matched to a controller route); the other 45 are captured call sites, 18 configuration-bound HTTP client calls and 27 broker publishes. The 45 sites yield 51 edges because a broker publish fans out to every cross-member subscriber. READ THE 51 WITH ITS DATE: it was 15 on the 2026-09-13 index and 0 before S-397 T1, and the whole of the move is index-time capture arriving, not a change in this tier's rule. WHAT THE 51 IS NOT, restated because the previous generation of this line said the opposite: it is no longer true that the bridge draws no invocation edge for these rows. Until S-420 (CR-133) the bridge keyed an HTTP consumer on its RAW ledger target, so `logos xservice route-providers` returned 81 edges, all contract-surface, and `coverage.bridge_invocation_edges` read 0 for that arm. Both arms now key on the committed value: the same command returns 132 edges, 51 of them invocation (33 broker-topic, 18 route), and the rider reads 51. The two figures still answer different questions — a fan-out publish is one resolution and many edges, an ambiguous composition is one resolution and none — and neither is folded into the other. NO FLOOR IS ASSERTED ON ANY OF THESE FIGURES.

S-374.story: The HTTP client-call arm records its refusals
S-374.effect: NOW OBSERVED. The 2026-09-13 re-index wrote 131 route/invocation rows where the 1.4.7 store held 1 — the workspace-wide figure S-374 recorded, landing at the upper end of the predicted 115-131 range exactly as the prediction said an index run would. 87 of them are `base-url-runtime` refusals and the other 44 are S-397 T1's configuration-bound rows, so the `unbound` column rose by 87 rather than by 131: the prediction's magnitude is confirmed and its split was not foreseen, because S-397 T1 had not been written when it was made. `egress_resolution_measured` 54 -> 155 and `spec_conformance_measured` 282 -> 383; `spec_conformance_ratio` 0.287 -> 0.225. `resolved_cross_service_edges` stayed 0 as predicted.

S-375.story: The client-call detector gate is receiver-grained, not file-grained
S-375.effect: ZERO change to every figure here, and that zero is a measured result rather than an absence. The narrowing removed 4 Java sites, all verified false positives (three list-index accesses and a cookie-map put), none of which emitted a reference: the workspace-wide genuine `http-client-call` reference count is 1 before and 1 after. Its real effect is on S-374's denominator on the NEXT index: against a file-grained gate, refusal recording would have written 4 ledger rows for a list index and a cookie put, so the range above would have been 4 rows wider at each end — the 'manufactures a coverage denominator out of ordinary code' hazard CR-120 §7 names, avoided.
S-375.evidence: sprint-impl-66.md, S-375 reference-workspace measurement table (before/after 98 -> 94 Java sites, 1 -> 1 workspace emitted)

S-377.story: Coverage reports its intake on every row
S-377.effect: Additive to the payload, and it moves NO count: `intake` became unconditional on all 929 rows (848 of which carried none) and the `by_intake` block was added, derived from the same tally the four headline counters are now derived from. It is what makes this baseline's decisive figure legible at all — `by_intake.invocation.bound: 0` beside a headline `bound: 81`. Measured payload cost on the reference workspace's shape: +2.9% compact bytes.

S-376.story: Retire the bound-ratio; the headline is a resolved-edge count (this story)
S-376.effect: Observed ON THE 1.4.7 GENERATION, which is where this delta was measured and where its figures belong: over that generation it renamed three summary fields and added four, moving no classification count — `bound_ratio 0.287` became `spec_conformance_ratio 0.287` with its composed line byte-identical, and the new headline read `resolved_cross_service_edges: 0` with `egress_resolution: 0.000 (0 of 54 egress sites resolved)`. Those two figures are NOT the measurement block above, which is the 2026-09-13 generation (0.225 of 383, and 0.032 of 155); the rename this delta describes is unaffected by the re-index, and the field names it introduced are the ones the block above uses. Measured payload cost on the reference workspace's shape: under 0.1% compact bytes, all of it on the summary object and none per-row.

S-397.story: The accessor capture hop reaches the invocation arm
S-397.effect: The whole of the invocation column's bound and ambiguous halves on the FIRST refresh: 0 -> 5 bound and 0 -> 9 ambiguous, plus 30 `no-provider-in-workspace`, being the 44 rows that carried `config-bound` provenance where the 1.4.7 store carried none. It is also why the `unbound` rise was 87 and not 131 (see S-374). Those figures are superseded by the S-398/S-402 entries below, which re-measured the same column over a later index generation; they are kept because the delta they attribute is this story's and does not move. Measured against S-397 AC2's floor of 79 the 44 was a SHORTFALL, diagnosed in the evidence below as the qualified-receiver ceiling; this artifact records the payload effect, not the verdict.

S-398.story: The accessor hop reaches a qualified receiver (T1)
S-398.effect: TEN more egress sites bind: by_intake.invocation.bound 5 -> 15, and ambiguous 9 -> 23. The estate writes every accessor qualified (`this.mailboxApiProperties.getUriGetMailbox()`), which the pre-hop pipeline refused, so the rows exist in the ledger and now resolve. Combined with S-402's denominator correction this moves egress_resolution 0.032 -> 0.128. NOT attributable to S-403 T1, which changed no resolution behaviour.
S-398.evidence: sprint-impl-69.md, S-398 T1; measured here on the 2026-09-13 Iteration-1 index

S-402.story: The Go client-call gate is receiver-grained
S-402.effect: The egress DENOMINATOR falls: egress_resolution_measured 155 -> 117, and references 1060 -> 1034. 26 captured `r.Header.Get(k)`-shaped Go non-calls in `hermodr-mirror` stopped being captured (37 rows -> 11), every one of them an `unbound` / `base-url-runtime` row, so no bound row moved. Any egress figure quoted against the pre-correction 155 is quoted against a denominator that no longer exists.
S-402.evidence: sprint-impl-69.md, S-402 T1; measured here on the 2026-09-13 Iteration-1 index

S-399.story: The accessor hop reaches through a UriBuilder lambda
S-399.effect: OBSERVED at last on the 2026-09-17 re-enrolment, and it landed where the pending entry predicted. This entry was the only `pending-reindex` one in this artifact for four generations. Its prediction was THREE further egress sites resolving with the captured population unmoved, and the egress denominator holding at 117: both hold. The three sites the sprint review named on 2026-09-14 (funnel-aggregator-api MailboxApiRestClient.java:268, mailbox-aggregator-api ReportingApiRestClient.java:110 and :122) are among the +3 HTTP bound rows. RECORDED_ADMITTED in config_bound_admission.rs, which the pending entry said was expected to read ~84 and then ~90, reads 90. Not netted with the S-405 or broker-arm entries below.

S-403.story: The resolved-edge headline agrees with its payload (this story)
S-403.effect: `resolved_cross_service_edges` 0 -> 15 and `resolved_edges_summary` "0 resolved cross-service edges; egress resolution 0.032 (5 of 155 …)" -> "15 resolved cross-service edges; egress resolution 0.128 (15 of 117 egress sites resolved)". A REPORTING CORRECTION ONLY: no classification, no capture and no resolution changed, and every other cell of the measurement block is identical with and without it — verified by reading the same store with and without the change. The superseded counter excluded `config-bound` rows so that it would stand in for the count of edges the BRIDGE drew; that is a real quantity under the wrong name, and it is now published as `coverage.bridge_invocation_edges` on the reachability rider, where it reads 0. This delta must not be mined as a capability gain.

S-405.story: A path-neutral composer link resolves on its path operand
S-405.effect: SIX further HTTP accessor sites present their configuration key on this generation — the `queryParam`-family residue S-399 left — which is why the HTTP arm's `config-bound` rows read 90 rather than 84. Of the nine S-399 and S-405 add between them, three land in `bound` and six in `ambiguous`, so the contribution to this file's headline is +3, not +9. Like S-399 it is a RESOLUTION, not a capture: the egress denominator does not move.

S-409/S-410.story: The accessor hop reaches the broker arm; topic identity is the committed configured value
S-409/S-410.effect: THE LARGEST SINGLE MOVEMENT IN THIS FILE'S HISTORY, and it is a new POPULATION rather than a better result on the old one. The broker arm gained committed-value topic resolution, so 27 broker publishes now bind where the payload previously carried none with `config-bound` provenance: by_intake.invocation.bound +27, and the arm's own `topic-not-literal` refusals fall 54 -> 27 inside the unchanged egress denominator. They contribute 33 EDGES, not 27, because one publish binds every cross-member subscriber. Any reading of `15 -> 45` as an improvement in HTTP egress resolution is wrong by 27 of the 30.

S-420.story: The bridge keys an HTTP consumer on its committed target
S-420.effect: ZERO change to every figure in this artifact, and the zero is a MEASURED result rather than an absence: the same estate was read on 2026-09-18 with and without the bridge arm and the two coverage payloads are byte-identical on every counter. It is recorded here because this file's headline sentence used to end with a claim S-420 falsified — that the bridge draws no invocation edge for these rows — and a delta table with no entry for the story that falsified it would leave the correction unattributed. What the story DOES move is coverage.bridge_invocation_edges, 33 -> 51, on the reachability rider; that figure is not in this artifact and its single home is config_bound_admission.rs. No floor is asserted on it.
